{"content": "### Add attestation step for container images

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/security-for-github-actions/using-artifact-attestations/using-artifact-attestations-to-establish-provenance-for-builds

Specify the image name and SHA256 digest. Set push-to-registry to true to attach the attestation to the image in the registry.

```yaml
- name: Generate artifact attestation
  uses: actions/attest@v4
  with:
    subject-name: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
    subject-digest: 'sha256:fedcba0...'
    push-to-registry: true

```

### Verify Artifact Attestation for Container Images using GitHub CLI

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations/use-artifact-attestations

This command verifies artifact attestations for container images using the GitHub CLI. It requires logging into `ghcr.io` first and providing the image's FQDN prefixed with `oci://`. Replace placeholders with your organization, image name, and repository.

```bash
docker login ghcr.io

gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/ORGANIZATION_NAME/IMAGE_NAME:test -R ORGANIZATION_NAME/REPOSITORY_NAME
```

### Using Artifact Attestations to Establish Provenance for Builds > Generating Artifact Attestations for Your Builds > Generating Build Provenance for Container Images

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations/use-artifact-attestations

To generate build provenance for container images, you need to configure permissions including id-token write, contents read, attestations write, and packages write access. After building the container image, you use the attest action with subject-name (the fully-qualified image name without a tag), subject-digest (the SHA256 digest of the image), and push-to-registry set to true. The subject-digest can be obtained from the digest output of docker/build-push-action, allowing you to create a verifiable attestation for your container image.

--------------------------------

### About Image Verification > Generating Attestations

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/kubernetes-admissions-controller

In order for an image to be verifiable, it must have a valid provenance attestation in the registry, which can be done by enabling the `push-to-registry: true` attribute in the `actions/attest` action. This generates the necessary build provenance for container images that the Policy Controller can verify during image pull requests.", "results": []}
